strategy.summary: Reproduce the pandas Timedelta bug where non-finite floats and overflowing round floats/ints with coarse units raise a bare OverflowError instead of OutOfBoundsTimedelta. Build pandas from source at the buggy commit and run the two added test files; the target tests should fail on the buggy revision with OverflowError and pass on the fixed revision with OutOfBoundsTimedelta.

pip_packages: cython (unpinned; the README documents it without a constraint)
numpy (unpinned; documented in README, no version constraint, so choose a current release compatible with this checkout)
system_packages: a C compiler toolchain able to build pandas Cython extensions (gcc or clang, plus make)

strategy.test_command: python -m pytest pandas/tests/scalar/timedelta/test_constructors.py pandas/tests/tools/test_to_timedelta.py -k 'float_inf_raises or round_float_overflow_unit or object_inf' -q
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 20542d17b1cc the selected tests FAIL: Timedelta(np.inf) and to_timedelta(np.inf) raise a bare OverflowError from int(item), which is not an OutOfBoundsTimedelta (a ValueError), so pytest.raises(OutOfBoundsTimedelta, match='without overflow') does not match and the test fails. On the fixed revision (the PR head) the same selected tests PASS: non-finite floats raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta with message containing 'without overflow', errors='coerce' returns NaT, and Timedelta(1e19, unit='s') and Timedelta(10**19, unit='s') raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta.
strategy.numerical_probe: Type of the exception raised by Timedelta(np.inf) and to_timedelta(np.inf, errors='coerce') on each revision: OverflowError on buggy, OutOfBoundsTimedelta / NaT on fixed.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: bare OverflowError (not caught, NaT not returned)

risks: The bug is a Python-level exception-type issue, so it should reproduce on any platform, but the test only transitions if the buggy commit is built with the same compiled extensions as the fixed one; rebuild after checking out each revision.

The message match 'without overflow' depends on the fixed code's wrapper message around np.timedelta64 casting; the message text is only partially given in the evidence, so a mismatch would appear as a failure on the fixed revision too.

The NumPy version is not documented or era-constrained; the overflow path for Timedelta(1e19, unit='s') goes through np.timedelta64(value, unit), whose exact behaviour may vary across NumPy releases. Pick one NumPy release and keep it fixed for both revisions.

The test files may need OutOfBoundsTimedelta and NaT and to_timedelta imported; if the buggy revision's test module lacks these imports the tests would error for an unrelated reason. Verify the imports before trusting a failure.
Test files may depend on hypothesis or other dev dependencies imported by pandas conftest; install the pandas test requirements if collection fails.
The Python version is not stated in the evidence (python_version null); use a Python version supported by the checked-out pandas revision.
Python version and platform are not constrained by the evidence; no sanitizer, architecture or threading condition is indicated, so no special platform is assumed.

oracle.reference_source: pandas/tests/scalar/timedelta/test_constructors.py and pandas/tests/tools/test_to_timedelta.py as added by the PR diff
oracle.why: The transition is decided by exception type (OutOfBoundsTimedelta, a ValueError, versus bare OverflowError) and by the NaT return under errors='coerce'; no numerical tolerance applies.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: Timedelta(np.inf) raises a bare OverflowError from int(item); pytest.raises(OutOfBoundsTimedelta, match='without overflow') does not catch it because OverflowError is not a subclass of OutOfBoundsTimedelta, so the test fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: The fix uses is_integer() so non-finite floats fall through to _numeric_to_td64ns and raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta with the expected message, errors='coerce' returns NaT, and the wrapped np.timedelta64 cast raises OutOfBoundsTimedelta for 1e19 and 10**19 with unit='s'; all assertions hold.
